transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 mins (recording started)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Cinder Lead Eng), Sara Nguyen (Platform), Noah Patel (DevOps)

Summary:
Quickwalk: SDK install (py/ts), auth methods (API key vs SSO), env var patterns, sandbox creds, and a short baseline plan for latency/cost. Customer asked about Private/VPC and KMS.

Topics: SDK setup, auth strategies, multiple envs (dev/stage/prod), sample prompt batching, KV cache mention, console walkthrough, Optimize suggestions.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call. I'm Maya from Redwood, Jordan from our infra team is with me.
[00:08] Liam: Hi yeah Liam here, Sara and Noah from Cinder too. Thanks for doing this on short notice.
[00:12] Jordan: Cool, we planned to go through the Python and TS SDK quickstart, show auth options, then hop into the console and Optimize recommendations. Please interrupt.
[00:21] Liam: Sounds good. Our primary goal is to get a dev sandbox working and then run a small cost/latency baseline to see if hosted is viable before we think about Dedicated.
[00:29] Sara: And from security side we need to confirm KMS support and audit log retention, plus SSO for the team.
[00:34] Maya: Sure. We'll cover each. Just to check, you currently use AWS and GCP for infra?
[00:38] Noah: Mostly AWS, some infra in GCP for analytics. We'll likely need VPC peering if we go Private later.
[00:44] Maya: Noted.

--- SDK install + Auth demo ---
[00:50] Jordan: Alright jumping into code. For Python pip install redwood-inference (note: package names in demo are illustrative). Example snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then client.generate(...). For TypeScript it's similar with import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'.
[01:12] Liam: Quick question — can we use short-lived tokens via our SSO or do we have to store long-lived keys?
[01:16] Jordan: You can do both. Hosted API supports API keys as the simplest path. For enterprise customers we support SAML/SSO and OIDC provisioning to mint short-lived tokens. Also there is an option for instance-level service tokens for Dedicated.
[01:31] Sara: Are those service tokens integrated with KMS? We need keys not stored in plaintext in the console.
[01:35] Maya: Yes — for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS; hosted uses our managed key but we can integrate with your KMS via a bring-your-own-key flow for certain enterprise tiers. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[01:47] Noah: Good. For sandbox do you give us temporary creds?
[01:50] Maya: We'll provision sandbox creds — short-lived API keys scoped to the sandbox project. I'll attach them to an email and the sample repo.

[02:05] Jordan: Also a note about env patterns: we recommend REDWOOD_API_KEY in secrets manager and then env var per environment: REDWOOD_API_KEY_DEV, _STAGE, _PROD. Avoid committing keys to repo. We showed a GitHub Actions snippet for rotating keys.
[02:26] Liam: Cool.

--- Console walkthrough + Optimize ---
[02:30] Maya: Switching to Console — quick tour: model catalog, per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, and Optimize suggestions. If you upload a small prompt set we can pro-actively recommend batching and quantization profiles.
[02:45] Sara: How does Optimize recommend quantization vs accuracy tradeoffs? We can't degrade customer-facing UX.
[02:51] Jordan: Optimize produces recommended profiles with expected latency/cost deltas and a small eval on your prompt set. You can set an SLA floor so recommendations that reduce quality below that threshold are filtered out.
[03:07] Liam: Are those evals run in prod or in a staging replica?
[03:11] Jordan: Staging replicas — we run the evals on compatible model variants to estimate. For highest fidelity we can run a small A/B test against real traffic during a pilot.

--- Technical constraints discussion ---
[03:22] Sara: We have strict data residency for EU customers. Does hosted support region pinning?
[03:27] Maya: Yes, hosted can pin region and we have EU regions. For absolute residency requirements we recommend Private in-region deployment.
[03:36] Noah: On network — if we move to Private, how's VPC set up? Do you support VPC peering or Transit?
[03:42] Jordan: We do VPC peering and private links. On-prem option exists but requires more setup. We'll share the network topology doc.
[03:50] Liam: Latency target for us is sub-250ms 95th for simple completions at 512 tokens. Is that realistic on hosted?
[03:58] Jordan: It depends on model and load. For smaller open models with quantized variants and batching tuned you can often hit that; for larger models Dedicated with pinned GPUs is safer. We'll run the baseline tests and give a realistic SLO suggestion.

--- Live code hiccup and transcription noise ---
[04:12] Jordan: I'm going to run the small Python example now, please watch the terminal.
[04:16] (brief typing)
[04:20] Jordan: Hmm getting an auth error — looks like the env var didn't pick up on this shell. Sorry — user error.
[04:25] Liam: No worries, that's the kind of stuff we expect.

--- Objections and tradeoffs ---
[04:30] Sara: One concern is cost predictability. We'll need to understand worst-case token spend for spikes and also how to cap usage per route.
[04:38] Maya: Console supports per-route quotas and token budgets. You can also set fallbacks to smaller models if budget is hit. We can show configuration examples.
[04:47] Liam: Is there rate limiting at the account level or per-key?
[04:50] Jordan: Both. Rate limits can be set per API key and per-route. For Dedicated we can provide throughput guarantees.

--- Security / Compliance quick Qs ---
[04:58] Sara: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation?
[05:01] Maya: Yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. We will share certs and your security checklist.
[05:07] Sara: Audit logs — retention options and export?
[05:10] Jordan: Console exposes audit logs and you can export to your SIEM. Retention is configurable depending on tier; for Private you control retention.

--- Recap & Next steps ---
[05:20] Maya: Recap: we'll share SDK sample repo, sandbox creds, KMS/Network docs, and a baseline plan. Jordan will run latency baseline with 10 prompts and upload results. Liam will confirm security contact. Target to start pilot the week of 2025-06-09.
[05:36] Liam: That works. Thanks.
[05:39] Noah: Appreciate the call — we'll try the sample this week.
[05:42] Maya: Great, I'll drop items into an email and create a shared board for the pilot.
[05:46] Sara: One last thing — can you include the short-run pricing assumptions for hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:51] Maya: Yep we'll include a pricing sheet with sample math for 100k tokens/day.

(Recording ends)
